newsitem.title: UK: International LPG listless, most markets steady.
newsitem.headline: International LPG listless, most markets steady.

text.p: International liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) markets were languishing in the summer doldrums this week, with trade generlly sluggish.
In the Far East, confusion over Saudi Aramco's September loading programme stalled business, with traders waiting for clarification before stepping into the market.
Saudi Aramco had released fob allocations at both Ras Tanura in the Gulf and Yanbu on the Red Sea and traders said it was still unclear exactly how many cargoes were available for Far East buyers.

"There's confusion over the loading programme. It's still not possible to identify whether there are surplus cargoes or not...by next Monday the problem may be resolved," said one trader active in Far East market.
Fob differentials were notionally pegged little changed at Saudi Contract Price (CP) minus $5/$10 a tonne for propane and CP parity to minus $5 for butane.
Prices for delivered material were also steady on the week. A 50:50 propane/butane cargo for September 9-10 delivery was sold into Japan at CP plus $15 a tonne on a C+F basis.
European traders were equally unenthusiastic with prices moving little over the course of the week.
